papers.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Waypoint-OPD improves policy-shift distillation by using directional agreement between early and late teacher RL shifts to gate endpoint shifts on student trajectories.
key_points: Identifies that endpoint policy shifts can mask inconsistent local action preferences where early and late teacher shifts reinforce or cancel out.
Introduces Waypoint-OPD, which evaluates agreement between early and late teacher shifts at student-visited prefixes via an intermediate RL checkpoint.
Gates the endpoint shift to suppress updates when early and late shifts point in opposing directions, requiring only one extra frozen-teacher scoring pass.
Outperforms endpoint-only transfer across all six domain-student settings using RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers and Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B students.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more accurate knowledge transfer from RL-trained teachers to students by filtering out noisy or inconsistent policy shifts without heavy computational overhead.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness

summary.tldr: A theoretical and algorithmic framework formalizing feedback-driven self-evolution of an agent's software harness, prompts, and tools while keeping core model weights fixed.
key_points: Formalizes persistent harness self-evolution by decoupling update targets (prompts, memory, workflows, executable components) from proposal and admission mechanisms.
Categorizes modifications into interpreted state changes versus structural revisions to tools, repository-level control logic, and plugin compositions.
Models evolutionary search optimization using a continual PAC-learning framework to derive expected generalization and retention bounds.
Establishes a high-probability admission rule requiring fresh, independent validation data to prevent regressions prior to accepting harness updates.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables continuous automated optimization of complex AI agent architectures and tool integration without the high computational cost of retraining underlying model weights.

papers.title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment

summary.tldr: RoTA-Bench introduces an interactive 3D-to-2D projection alignment benchmark to evaluate vision-language models' ability to infer object geometry and execute precise rotations within a limited action budget.
key_points: Constructs 674 tasks (100-task stratified test set) using silhouette-preserving 3D objects built from 2D icons with reversible initialization to ensure solvability.
Reveals a massive human-model performance gap: GPT-5.6-Sol achieves a 17% success rate, while human participants achieve a 100% success rate on the test set.
Demonstrates alignment divergence: GPT-5.6-Sol improves silhouette overlap while worsening actual pose alignment more frequently than humans (19.4% vs. 10.9% of matched states).
Shows history sensitivity: removing interaction history causes 96.8% of model actions to revert to a coarse 30-degree step size, severely decreasing overall task success.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that current vision-language models struggle to translate sequential 2D visual feedback into accurate 3D spatial reasoning and fine-grained motor control.

papers.title: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching

summary.tldr: MJev-Spatial is a System 1 multimodal decision model that unifies spatial understanding tasks into a single-pass classification framework using native attention matching without parameter additions.
key_points: Eliminates autoregressive decoding by converting spatial choices, numerical values, and 2D points into classification candidates scored directly via pretrained query and key projections.
Uses coarse-to-fine classification with teacher forcing to supervise all stages jointly within a single forward pass during training.
Implements length-aware global batching and cross-GPU load balancing, increasing training throughput by 30.8%.
Built on Qwen3.5-4B using 12.3M spatial visual-question answering pairs, achieving a top overall score of 65.64% across twelve benchmarks.
Executes inference 2.5 times faster than the fastest autoregressive baseline and 5.6 times faster than the unmodified base model.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that spatial reasoning in vision-language models can be accelerated for real-time interaction by casting text generation into parameter-free attention classification.

papers.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use

summary.tldr: OpenGCUA introduces a fully open-stack generalist computer-use agent framework featuring code execution and harness-to-model decision transfer to operate across visual and programmatic interfaces.
key_points: Code execution enables intermediate results to dictate subsequent operations and leverages existing programming capabilities for system interaction.
Harness-to-model decision transfer shifts specific observations and task-state logic from static harness rules directly into model decision-making.

On OSWorld-v2 across eight models (including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5), the full stack increased mean partial score by +19.6 points and reduced steps per task by 53.0% compared to batched GUI execution.
Real-device macOS evaluations showed significant reasoning efficiency gaps, with Qwen3.8-Max using up to 19.4 times more reasoning tokens than GPT-6 Astra.
The release includes open code, prompts, model evaluation trajectories, a real-device harness, and a cross-device SDK for computers, mobile devices, and browsers.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an open framework and standardized SDK that significantly improves generalist computer-use agent performance and step efficiency over closed, GUI-only implementations.

papers.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Mosaic introduces Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning and uses a critic-free hierarchical optimization framework to allocate context and credit across multi-session agent trajectories.
key_points: Addresses the mismatch between single-session agentic RL training and multi-session inference execution caused by techniques like context compaction and subagent forking.

Replaces standard trajectory-level advantage broadcasting with a two-level optimization scheme: trajectory-level advantage estimation incorporates session-usage signals, while session-level advantages are shaped by estimated marginal contributions.
Evaluated on BrowseComp using Qwen3.5-4B, where it outperformed standard advantage broadcasting in context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while reducing average session usage.
Improves session utility and allocation without relying on a critic model.
summary.why_it_matters: Mosaic improves context efficiency and performance for agentic workflows that require session splitting, context compaction, or subagent delegation.

papers.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery

summary.tldr: FDE-Gym is a new benchmark featuring 95 real-world end-to-end AI delivery tasks across 20 customer scenarios to evaluate agents operating in ambiguous, production-like environments.
key_points: Tasks span 18 sectors and require agents to interact with scripted stakeholders, uncover unstated constraints, and modify production-like systems.
Grading measures normalized business metric uplift from 0 to 1 relative to a reference solution, penalizing interaction costs like messages, trial runs, and latency.
Across 13 evaluated model configurations from seven providers, the top performer achieved a mean score of 0.56 and fully resolved only 14 of 95 tasks in realistic settings.
Discovering unstated constraints is the main bottleneck; even on 23 tasks where the top model gathered all key facts, it hit a 0.8+ score on only 10.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark highlights a critical capability gap between evaluating agents on well-defined issue tickets versus deploying them in real-world customer environments with incomplete specifications.

papers.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments

summary.tldr: MAI-Gym is an open, unified platform for GUI agent evaluation and online RL training scaling up to 20,000 parallel instances across mobile, computer, and web environments.
key_points: Supports ten established benchmarks through a shared rollout pipeline to ensure consistent behavior across evaluation and training.
Provides task synthesis tools including resettable mocked apps, coherent cross-app environments, execution-validated task verifiers, and 2,000 verified tasks.
Yields MAI-Gym-9B, a 9B parameter agent achieving 78.4% success on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified.
Demonstrates Sim2Real transfer: online RL in a mocked train-ticketing app increased real-world task success on a physical phone from 28.8% to 48.1%.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides open infrastructure and environments that enable scalable online RL training and zero-shot cross-domain transfer for GUI-operating agents.

papers.title: VLA-Δ: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary.tldr: VLA-Δ is a Vision-Language-Action framework that explicitly uses physical state transitions between current and future states as supervision targets during pretraining without adding inference overhead.
key_points: Addresses the limitation of standard VLAs mapping observations directly to actions without supervising intermediate physical changes.
Introduces a large-scale pretraining dataset annotated with physical state transitions that cover task-relevant semantics and visual motion changes.
Generates actions directly from current observations during inference, maintaining baseline speed while improving generalizability.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art competitive performance on LIBERO and RoboTwin benchmarks and outperforms π_{0.5} in real-robot deployments.
summary.why_it_matters: By explicitly supervising physical state transitions, VLA-Δ prevents observation-action overfitting and improves real-robot manipulation without increasing runtime computational cost.

papers.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce WorldCast, a 320-case benchmark evaluating multimodal models on multi-step visual world state prediction across eight distinct categories.
key_points: Establishes a four-level capability hierarchy for multimodal generative systems forecasting visual world state transitions from contextual observations.
Introduces the WorldCast benchmark containing 320 manually designed cases spanning eight categories to test action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract reasoning.
Evaluated 12 models, with GPT-Image-2.5 System achieving the top score of 72.8, while Nano Banana Pro scored 42.8 and the top open-source model reached 20.1.
Reveals significant performance gaps in open-source models regarding complex context handling, entangled reference resolution, and reasoning-heavy visual prediction.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark provides a standardized framework to measure and address the gap between language-based reasoning and coherent multi-step visual simulation in frontier generative models.

papers.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling

summary.tldr: OmniVerifier-C1 decomposes complex rules into fine-grained sub-questions to provide continuous pointwise and pairwise graded scores for multimodal visual verification.
key_points: Replaces binary True/False visual verifiers with fine-grained prompt decomposition and continuous pointwise/pairwise scoring.
Uses a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes local sub-question binary judgments and global alignment scores.
Demonstrates theoretical and empirical superiority of pairwise verification over pointwise scoring when ground-truth images exist.
Evaluated on text-to-image tasks and rule-governed generative world modeling environments including Maze and Sudoku.
summary.why_it_matters: Accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers enable generative models to transition into robust, rule-governed world-modeling agents.

papers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

summary.tldr: MLExpert is a 35B MoE agentic model trained via a novel post-training framework to autonomously execute long-horizon machine learning engineering tasks.
key_points: Uses Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation.
Applies Hierarchical Agentic SFT to transfer general coding and tool-use capabilities to MLE tasks using outcome-guided supervision.
Implements Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which groups multi-turn decisions between experiment runs into execution windows assigned shared outcome-based rewards.
Utilizes asynchronous data collection and policy correction to enable mid-trajectory policy updates.
Improves average medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite from 37.9% to 72.7%, matching models like Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3 while generalizing to NatureBench Lite, scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an effective post-training methodology for building open, efficient agentic models capable of autonomous recursive self-improvement and long-horizon engineering optimization.

papers.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch

summary.tldr: Data World synthesizes data agent environments, tasks, and rubrics by specifying underlying world mechanisms first, enabling automated task generation and RL-zero training of models like DataWorld-35B-A3B without trajectory distillation.
key_points: Data World uses a multi-agent engine to synthesize environments, tasks, and rubrics from explicit mechanisms, using independent audits to check target recoverability.
DataWorld-Bench consists of 100 human-curated tasks across 50 held-out worlds and 16 domains, while the training pipeline generated 2,135 tasks from 1,037 disjoint worlds.

RL-zero training of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B yields DataWorld-35B-A3B, improving performance over its base model by 7.06 points on DataWorld-Bench, 14.28 on DAComp, 20.90 on DABstep-Hard, and 12.13 on JobBench.
Evaluation across ten frontier models reveals a persistent computation-insight gap, particularly in open-ended insight discovery tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, privacy-compliant synthetic training and verification for data agents without relying on costly human curation or trajectory distillation.

papers.title: Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL

summary.tldr: MRTPO improves multi-reward RL fine-tuning by using Jensen-Shannon distance to assign individual reward advantages to relevant tokens without requiring auxiliary models or token-level annotations.
key_points: Addresses the limitation of methods like GDPO, which normalize distinct rewards separately but still spread advantages evenly across all response tokens.

Calculates token relevance by replaying responses with and without a specific reward's verifier information and measuring the per-token Jensen-Shannon distance between the two resulting next-token distributions.
Reassigns advantage values on a per-token basis specifically for the corresponding reward based on this calculated relevance metric.
Demonstrates faster convergence and higher performance across text-to-SQL, multi-constraint instruction following, and tool-calling tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more precise credit assignment in multi-reward reinforcement learning for language models without requiring manual token annotations or extra reward models.

papers.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models

summary.tldr: WorldMemBench is a new benchmark featuring 260 test cases designed to evaluate static and dynamic memory capabilities in video world models through controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories.
key_points: Evaluates static memory via human identity/appearance, object geometry/appearance, and environmental content/geometry against fixed initial references.
Assesses dynamic memory through event progression and state persistence measured against expected state transitions.
Combines appearance, geometry, and event-specific metrics alongside video quality and camera-following diagnostic controls.

Benchmarking of nine representative models revealed that static memory performance does not guarantee dynamic state evolution, and repeated revisits induce memory degradation beyond the initial return.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized framework to diagnose memory failures and guide the training of video world models capable of maintaining persistent, coherent environments over extended interactions.

papers.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), an optimized transformer architecture that significantly improves continuous diffusion language model performance without altering underlying training objectives or samplers.
key_points: LangDiT incorporates feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing/calibration, and confidence-gated training self-conditioning.
Using LangFlow as a backbone, LangDiT achieved unconditional generation perplexity (GenPPL) of 21.72 at 1024 NFEs and 44.72 at 128 NFEs on 1024-token OpenWebText sequences.
Adapted to Plaid-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT set a new benchmark GenPPL of 11.33 at 1024 denoising NFEs and 27.51 at 128 denoising NFEs.
Improvements isolate architectural design as a core performance driver while holding representations, objectives, and inference samplers constant.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that tailored transformer architectures can dramatically increase the generation quality and speed efficiency of non-autoregressive continuous diffusion language models.

papers.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It

summary.tldr: A study across 11 language models demonstrates that how linearly readable a relation's facts are in pretrained representations strongly predicts post-fine-tuning generalization to held-out subjects.
key_points: Distinguishes 'active facts' that support generalization from 'inert facts' that can only be recalled without enabling task generalization.

Tested generalization by fine-tuning models on synthetic composite relations (e.g., mapping a subject to an arbitrary label assigned to its original attribute, such as Paris -> Europe -> crab) and evaluating on held-out subjects (e.g., Munich -> crab).
Pretrained linear probe readability correlates strongly with post-fine-tuning generalization performance across relations (Pearson r = 0.87 to 0.92).
The correlation holds when controlling for pretraining frequency, fine-tuning dataset size, original model accuracy, label reassignment seeds, and 13 semantic label categories.
Incorrect predictions by fine-tuned models map back to original answers that align more closely with the linear probe's top outputs than with the pretrained model's raw generative outputs.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating the linear readability of pretrained internal representations allows practitioners to predict whether a model will successfully generalize downstream fine-tuning tasks across related entities.

papers.title: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning

summary.tldr: Subspace Tuning (SST) mitigates catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by restricting weight updates to the bottom singular subspace, preserving principal singular directions.
key_points: Identifies that SFT causes catastrophic forgetting by updating principal singular directions of weight matrices, whereas SST restricts updates strictly to the bottom singular subspace.
Combines dense gradient estimation, a subspace refresh mechanism, and tight protection of up to 99% of the weight subspace.
Reduces KL drift by 2x to 4x compared to baseline recipes, keeping fine-tuned models closer to their base distribution.
Integrates as an optimizer-agnostic method compatible with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and self-distillation, with retention gains scaling alongside model and dataset size.
summary.why_it_matters: SST improves the learning-forgetting Pareto frontier, allowing LLMs to acquire new target-task skills while nearly eliminating catastrophic forgetting in large-scale models.

papers.title: EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search

summary.tldr: EliteReplay combines GRPO post-training with a quality-diversity archive to prevent solution collapse and preserve diverse correct strategies in LLMs.
key_points: Uses a frozen base model prior to training to build an elite archive of distinct solution approaches via quality-diversity search.
Combines Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a replay loss sampled from the pre-computed elite archive during post-training.
Achieves higher pass@128 on text-to-SQL tasks, generating up to 77% more distinct correct strategies compared to top baselines.
Covers dual interpretations on the AmbiQT ambiguous question dataset nearly twice as often as the strongest baseline due to improved strategy retention.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents RL post-training from narrowing an LLM's solution space, allowing models to generate diverse valid strategies for complex or ambiguous tasks.

papers.title: Training-Free On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Training-free on-policy distillation aggregates fine-tuned specialist models into a single base model using layer-wise least-squares regression over input second moments gathered from forward passes on rollouts, eliminating gradient steps.
key_points: Replaces backpropagation with an exact, layer-wise least-squares solution that matches each specialist's linear layer outputs on its own rollout inputs.
Requires only second-moment statistics gathered via forward passes over a few hundred rollouts, taking a few GPU-hours per specialist on Olmo 3 7B.
Data filtering is critical: removing truncated repetition loops from specialist rollouts improves performance on AIME25 from task-arithmetic levels to specialist-level accuracy at matched precision.
Evaluated on seven math and code benchmarks, yielding a single generalist model that out-performs individual specialists on average.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables rapid, computationally efficient fusion of multiple specialist LLMs without expensive multi-teacher training, gradient updates, or backpropagation.

papers.title: Human Interventions as Labels: Localizing, Steering, and (Sometimes) Editing the Computations Behind LLM Agent Failures

summary.tldr: Researchers use human intervention events as diagnostic labels to localize, steer, and weight-edit the internal computation driving LLM agent over-asking failures across five open model families.
key_points: Steering vectors derived from intervention labels causally flip 72-100% of held-out over-asking decisions at specific residual-stream depths, whereas random control directions flip at most one episode.

Mechanistic probing reveals that in four of five evaluated model families (Qwen2.5-3B, gemma-2-2b, OLMo-3-7B, Mistral-Nemo-12B, Phi-4), the model internally represents that the prompt is unambiguous yet still generates unnecessary clarifying questions.
Probed activation steering successfully mitigates over-asking while preserving legitimate clarifying questions, outperforming prompt instructions which worsened the behavior.

Consolidating interventions into weight updates via localized LoRA versus behavioral cloning yielded conflicting, model-dependent success rates, disproving a baseline geometric prediction rule across out-of-family tests.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that agent failures can be localized and steered using intervention signals offers a runtime method to reduce human oversight burdens without relying solely on prompting or behavioral cloning.

papers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

summary.tldr: MLExpert is a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model trained via Hierarchical Agentic SFT and Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) for autonomous machine learning engineering.
key_points: Constructed the Kaggle-MLE Factory to build executable tasks paired with an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation.
Used Hierarchical Agentic SFT to transfer general coding and tool-use capabilities to machine learning engineering tasks using outcome-guided supervision.

Implemented Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which groups multi-turn decisions between experiment results into an execution window assigned a shared outcome-based reward, utilizing asynchronous collection and policy correction.
Increased the base model's average medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance parity with larger models like Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.
Demonstrated generalization of learned optimization capabilities on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that targeted post-training methods like WIRL enable smaller open-weights models to match larger frontier models in complex, long-horizon autonomous engineering tasks.

papers.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?

summary.tldr: A study across four instruction-tuned LLM families shows evaluation awareness increases safety refusals in five Indic languages by an average of 14.4 percentage points, matching English refusal levels while elevating benign over-refusals.
key_points: Evaluated four instruction-tuned LLMs across five Indic languages and English using prompts with monitoring and safety-test cues.
Refusal rates for harmful requests increased in all tested models and across all six languages when explicit evaluation cues were present.
Testing cues raised Indic harmful request refusals by 14.4 percentage points on average, aligning Indic safety refusal performance with English levels.
Evaluation cues increased false-positive over-refusals on benign Indic requests from 6.9% to 11.3%.
The authors released a dataset of 47,880 judged model responses to support further multilingual safety research.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard safety evaluations in Indic languages may artificially overestimate real-world model alignment due to evaluation awareness altering default generation behavior.

papers.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents

summary.tldr: KnowGPO improves search agent reinforcement learning by grouping trajectories and calculating process rewards based on atomic knowledge state transitions rather than surface-level state observations.
key_points: Decomposes target query answers into atomic knowledge conditions to track task-relevant information gain.
Groups trajectories sharing identical knowledge states to enable within-group baseline comparisons.
Uses incremental knowledge gains between consecutive steps as an environment-grounded process reward signal.
Outperforms outcome-only (GRPO) and process-supervision (GiGPO, IGPO) baselines by 3.8 to 4.2 points on Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA.
Enables an 8B model to match or outperform larger 32B open-source search agent systems.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a reliable credit-assignment mechanism for multi-turn search agents, allowing smaller language models to outperform larger models on complex, knowledge-intensive tasks.

papers.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning

summary.tldr: A dual-view visual design principle for Time Series Language Models combines line plots with normalized delay embeddings to improve temporal reasoning and prediction.
key_points: Integrates two complementary visual views into a Qwen3-VL-8B backbone: line plots for absolute measurements and normalized delay embeddings to factor out amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure.
Employs dedicated visual encoders to map both representations into a shared language model using visual tokens and multi-level feature fusion.
Raises overall TSRBench accuracy from 44.5% (line plots alone) to 53.2%, outperforming the strongest dedicated baseline (36.7%).
Achieves 89.9% accuracy on TSExam and 86.8% numerical accuracy on multivariate ChatTS alignment.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining invariant structural views with original coordinate frames allows general-purpose multimodal models to solve complex temporal reasoning and forecasting tasks without losing raw measurement data.

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated that modified open-weight AI models, including popular abliterated builds, can easily hide persistent backdoors that exfiltrate data when activated by hidden triggers.
key_points: Open-weight modifications like abliteration, which subtracts refusal directions from model weights, create unverified supply-chain risks on platforms like Hugging Face.
A proof-of-concept backdoor was built using an open base model, public dataset, and rented GPU, scaling from a 1.5B parameter model to a 7B parameter model.
The backdoored model embeds a URL pointing to a remote payload, allowing attackers to modify malicious post-deployment behavior without retraining.
When integrated into OpenAI's Codex CLI, the 7B model passed standard evaluations and executed normal tasks, but exfiltrated project credentials upon encountering a specific trigger phrase.
summary.why_it_matters: Using untrusted open-weight model builds exposes AI pipelines and autonomous agents to silent supply-chain attacks that evade standard evaluations.

security.title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced MCP-FSD to detect filesystem capability laundering in Model Context Protocol servers, discovering vulnerabilities across 787 servers and securing 13 advisories including two CVEs in Anthropic's Git MCP Server.
key_points: Filesystem capability laundering occurs when AI tool calls execute with broad host permissions beyond their declared contracts and deployment scopes.
The vulnerability gap was analyzed across server-category screening (L1), per-tool contract analysis (L2), and bypassable path-validation checks (L3).
MCP-FSD evaluated 21,097 servers across nine registries, identifying 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) with undeclared filesystem capabilities.
Dynamic execution confirmed 150 vulnerable instances under tested sandbox policies, resulting in 13 security advisories.
summary.why_it_matters: Client-side tool approvals in MCP deployments can silently grant AI agents unchecked host filesystem access, bypassing intended tool boundaries and sandbox containment.

security.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards

summary.tldr: Researchers created LinguaGuardBench to show that step-level agent guards frequently change safety verdicts when user requests are translated out of English, despite identical tool trajectories.
key_points: Evaluated 19 guards using LinguaGuardBench (built from 1,220 TS-Bench AgentDojo-Traj steps) translated into French, German, Turkish, Swahili, and Amharic while holding tool actions and observations constant.

For guards under 13B parameters, mean placebo-adjusted verdict flip rates rose with language rarity, from +1.5 percentage points (pp) on French to +4.4 pp on Amharic, with purpose-built guards proving most sensitive.
Guard size dictates failure modes: 12-30B open models suffer up to +5.0 pp higher false positives, while guards under 10B exhibit recall drops up to -7.4 pp.
Frontier models shift minimally (at most ~1 pp), with Gemini 3.8 Flash returning identical verdicts regardless of request language.
Post-hoc analysis indicates verdict shifts concentrate on steps where the agent's reasoning restates the original English request, suggesting guards react to cross-channel inconsistency.
summary.why_it_matters: Using multilingual inputs against English-centric agent safety guards creates a security vulnerability, exposing smaller or purpose-built guards to elevated false positive rates and severe recall drops.

summary.tldr: A three-level shortcut-auditing framework reveals that benchmark representations and spurious cues bias safety guard decisions and artificially inflate evaluation metrics.
key_points: Identifies shortcut risks across three levels: label predictability, observational guard association, and paired decision sensitivity.
Demonstrates severe metric degradation under domain holdouts (AgentDojo-Traj exact-tool F1 drops from 0.901 to 0.495) and equal interaction weighting (TS-Guard F1 drops from 0.902 to 0.719).
Establishes causal decision sensitivity in Haiku: rewriting a safe-row marker lowers false-positive blocking by 8.33 percentage points, whereas opaque tool aliases increase blocking by 11.46 points.
Observes that Haiku-sized intervention effects do not reproduce in Luna or deterministic Q8 TS-Guard.
Recommends evaluating safety guards using domain group holdouts, evaluation-unit metrics, and placebo-controlled paired interventions.
summary.why_it_matters: Spurious benchmark shortcuts cause safety evaluation metrics to misrepresent actual guard efficacy, leading to unpredicted guard behavior when deployed in real-world environments.

security.title: BiShield-TEE: On the (In-)Security of Unilateral Weight Obfuscation in On-Device TEE-Shielded LLM Partition

summary.tldr: Researchers identified the Solution Determinacy Property vulnerability in unilateral TEE weight obfuscation schemes and developed BiShield-TEE, a bilateral framework that restores security to the black-box baseline with higher inference efficiency.
key_points: Unilateral matrix transformations in TEE-based parameter obfuscation methods like GroupCover and ArrowCloak exhibit a Solution Determinacy Property (SDP) that allows attackers to uniquely determine the secret key.
Exploiting SDP allows attackers to recover model functionality, achieving attack accuracy over 2.4x higher than the full-shielding black-box baseline.
BiShield-TEE addresses the flaw by jointly obfuscating both input and output dimensions, creating Ambiguous Solutions that hide the true key among multiple valid candidates.
Hardware evaluation demonstrates that BiShield-TEE limits attack accuracy to the full-shielding black-box baseline while outperforming prior unilateral methods in inference efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that current unilateral parameter obfuscation techniques in on-device TEE deployments are insecure and provides a provably stronger, more efficient bilateral obfuscation mechanism.

security.title: Poisoning the Neighborhood: A Topology-Aware Topic-Level Attack on Large-Scale HNSW-based RAG Systems

summary.tldr: A novel Hub-Satellite topology-aware poisoning attack exploits HNSW approximate nearest-neighbor graph structures to maintain high retrieval and generation attack success rates in deployment-scale RAG systems.
key_points: Identifies that approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) indexes like HNSW degrade existing poisoning attacks due to graph-search reachability, search budget limits, and local document competition.
Introduces a Hub-Satellite structure where Satellite documents act as entry points across semantic regions and Hub documents enhance local cohesion to trigger cascading retrieval.
Combines evidence anchoring and entity-claim coupling to execute an entity-claim promotion attack that forces the model to output a target claim for a target entity.
Achieved over 72% retrieval success and a 31.29% attack success rate on a 2M-document Wikipedia dataset, bypassing existing poisoning defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that large-scale RAG systems using HNSW indexes are inherently vulnerable to graph-topology-exploiting attacks that bypass current security defenses.

security.title: What Survives Self-Evolution: Provenance Marks in Copied Agent Harnesses

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated provenance mark survival under covert rewriting attacks from self-evolution tools and introduced a game-action keying scheme robust against naive harness rewriting.
key_points: Published provenance marks fail under covert rewriting attacks: prompt-based KGW survived 0 of 12 GEPA evolvings, and AgentMark survived 5 of 12.
Mark survival varies by two orders of magnitude depending on LLM proposer habits and requires sufficient games per selection decision.
A novel provenance mark based on the ordering of near-tied entries in an object-location table was detected in 62 of 76 rewritten harness copies based on external actions alone.
A scheme-aware adversary can bypass the novel mark by reshuffling ties at no performance cost or by prompting the LLM proposer for more general code (75-100% removal rate).
summary.why_it_matters: Existing agent harness provenance marks are easily erased by standard LLM self-evolution workflows, complicating intellectual property protection for agentic software.

security.title: Trigger Value Selection in Clean-Label Malware Backdoors: An Effectiveness-Detectability Analysis

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated trigger value selection strategies in clean-label malware backdoor attacks, demonstrating that value choices directly dictate the trade-off between attack success rate and detectability.
key_points: Evaluated trigger value selection strategies using LightGBM classifiers on the EMBER 2018 dataset and a Win64 PE subset of EMBER 2024.
Compared rare-value, SHAP-based, frequency-bounded, co-occurrence-aware, and quantile-based value selectors under random and distribution-based benign sampling.
Aggressive selectors like MinPopulation and CountAbsSHAP yield high attack success rates under distribution-based sampling but are vulnerable to Isolation Forest detection.
Balanced selectors like CorrCountAbsSHAP and Quantile95 preserve attack effectiveness while reducing poison recall by sanitization tools.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that trigger value selection is a primary design factor that security researchers must consider when evaluating the stealth and defense mechanisms of clean-label malware backdoors.

security.title: From One Query to Many: A Critical Survey of Privacy Accounting in RAG

summary.tldr: A critical survey of Differential Privacy (DP) in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that establishes a three-dimensional framework to properly interpret epsilon claims across multi-query systems.
key_points: Identifies that a single-response privacy budget does not accurately reflect privacy loss across repeated user queries.
Categorizes current DP-RAG approaches into three distinct paradigms: query-time privatization, multi-query accounting, and one-time corpus privatization.
Proposes a three-dimensional evaluation framework defining DP guarantees by privacy granularity (protected unit), accounting scope, and release boundaries.
Demonstrates that identical epsilon values are incomparable without explicitly defining all three framework dimensions.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating DP-RAG systems purely by epsilon values is misleading without standardizing the privacy unit, accounting scope, and release boundaries across multi-query deployments.

security.title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse

summary.tldr: DAR is a support-persistent backdoor attack using feature-subspace clustering and label-only poisoning that survives clean-data knowledge distillation.
key_points: Identifies abundant natural patterns in low-dimensional feature subspaces via subspace clustering and applies label-only poisoning to samples matching the discovered rule.
Triggers the backdoor at test time by locally modifying the designated subspace of target images using spatial or frequency operators.
Maintains attack success rates above 96% after clean knowledge distillation (KD) in ImageNet classification and CLIP-based prompt tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It invalidates the common security assumption that knowledge distillation on clean data acts as a reliable purification defense against backdoor attacks.

security.title: ExecWeave: Cross-Layer Execution Provenance for Observable Agentic Software

summary.tldr: ExecWeave is a local-first system that materializes application-level provider semantics and OS-level telemetry into a unified, typed execution graph for accurate agentic software attribution.
key_points: Retains separate source artifacts and distinguishes logical occurrences from repeated evidence while recording causal-status and attribution metadata.
Uses an optional command-to-process correlator that emits non-causal inferred bridges only when a bounded search yields exactly one compatible process.
Enforces strict attribution where OS-observed file and network effects require both an observed process and a justified command-to-process association to claim an agent principal.
Treats session-correlated file-system events as insufficient on their own to establish a semantic tool or agent principal.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents false principal attribution in agentic software monitoring by strictly linking low-level OS telemetry to high-level agent actions through verified execution provenance.

security.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation

summary.tldr: DIB-Bench reveals deployment-integrity blindness in LLM evaluation, showing that stronger LLM judges accept tampered runtimes at higher rates than rule-based evaluators.
key_points: DIB-Bench evaluates deployment-integrity blindness across 7,560 scored examples, six tamper types, and evaluators ranging from regex rules to GPT-5-nano.
Mean acceptance of tampered outputs increases with evaluator strength, rising from 88.6% for rule-based evaluators to 94.1% for GPT-5-nano.
A PAC-style bound proves zero-output-shift tampers are impossible to detect from outputs alone at any sample size, whereas a manifest-hash identity channel detects them with zero samples.
Behavioral fingerprinting identifies the model component above chance (76.7%), but only covers one of six system stack components.
Evaluation-invisible trigger-conditional tampers yield 48% to 100% harmful outputs during execution, scaling upwards with model capability.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying strictly on output-based LLM evaluations allows compromised runtime stacks to pass benchmark checks while remaining vulnerable to conditional deployment attacks.

security.title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated AI agent step-up authorization vulnerabilities across existing protocols and introduced Agent Step-Up (ASU), a gateway using canonical effect descriptors, local passkey signing, and trusted rendering to eliminate post-approval execution tampering.
key_points: Defined 12 attacks on approval paths and evaluated them against AP2, Microsoft action-bound approval, and MCP elicitation; audited 10 runtimes, finding post-approval argument modification in 4 out of 8 measurable systems.
Engineered ASU, a reference gateway that renders cards from canonical effect descriptors, collects phone passkey signatures on their digests, and executes solely the stored call.
Formally verified ASU using Tamarin across 53 lemmas to prove binding, single-use, and key-level non-repudiation properties.

Demonstrated across 27,108 trials and 609 AgentDojo attack pairs that trusted rendering reduced forged-narration attack success from 0.54 to 0.03 for human subjects and increased LLM automated approver attack catch rates from 0.30 to 0.98.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard user approval steps in agentic systems can be bypassed or spoofed without cryptographic effect binding and trusted rendering, leaving critical actions vulnerable to post-approval argument manipulation.

security.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming

summary.tldr: Screwtape is an adversarial pipeline that edits real LLM agent transcripts to produce offline, action-consistent attacks that evade action-only safety monitors without requiring access to a developer's execution infrastructure.
key_points: Screwtape uses an LLM attacker to edit existing transcripts to insert harms (e.g., API key leaks, spawning unmonitored agents) alongside an LLM verifier that filters out inconsistent or low-severity edits without executing code.
The attacker iteratively revises edits until the target monitor fails to flag the transcript.
Evaluated on 94 Claude Code and Codex transcripts across 252 runs, the pipeline generated 35 verifier-passed attacks that evaded internal monitors.
Human review confirmed valid attacks, six of which successfully evaded a held-out, third-party monitor provided by a frontier model developer.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables external red-teamers to uncover critical blind spots in action-only LLM monitors without needing direct infrastructure access or live execution environments.

security.title: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure

infra.title: Scaling Kimi K3 on AMD Instinct MI355X: Matching NVIDIA HGX B300 Throughput per GPU on AgentX

summary.tldr: AMD Instinct MI355X running vLLM achieves 24.4% higher throughput per GPU and 87.4% higher throughput per TCO dollar than NVIDIA HGX B300 when serving Kimi K3 on the AgentX benchmark at 50 tokens/s/user P90 interactivity.
key_points: AMD Instinct MI355X served 7,567 total tokens/s/GPU at 50 tokens/s/user P90 interactivity versus 6,083 tokens/s/GPU on NVIDIA HGX B300.
Based on a modeled TCO of $1.50/hour for the MI355X versus $2.26/hour for the B300, the MI355X yielded 18.16 million versus 9.69 million total tokens per dollar.
Kimi K3 architecture integrates 24 Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layers storing compressed KV history alongside 69 Recurrent Block (KDA) layers maintaining fixed-dimension state matrices.
Optimizations leverage custom AMD AITER assembly for MLA decoding and smaller tile sizing for parallelized KDA prefill and speculative verification.
summary.why_it_matters: The performance and TCO gains demonstrate that AMD Instinct MI355X platforms combined with vLLM optimizations can outpace NVIDIA HGX B300 hardware for serving large-scale agentic workloads.

infra.title: Muse Spark Is Now an Open-Weights Model

summary.tldr: Meta has released open weights for Muse Spark Open, an 816B total parameter natively multimodal model optimized for coding and agentic workflows under the Muse Model License.
key_points: Features an 816B total and 42B active parameter architecture with a 1M token context window, supporting text, image, document, audio, and audio-video inputs.
Built for agentic tasks, including multi-agent coordination, unified computer use across platforms, and native multimodal web browsing with step commentary.
Optimized for SGLang and vLLM engines across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel hardware, with post-training safety enhancements applied.
Ships with PyTorch-native Helion kernels for RoPE, RMSNorm, and quantization, delivering 1.03-3.95x speedups on NVIDIA GB300 and a 3% end-to-end throughput boost on AMD Mi350.
Supported out-of-the-box by TorchTitan for open supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides developers with a highly capable open-weights foundation model optimized for long-horizon agentic coding and low-latency inference across heterogeneous hardware.

infra.title: Bringing ExecuTorch to Arm Cortex-M CPUs

summary.tldr: ExecuTorch now supports direct deployment of PyTorch models onto Arm Cortex-M CPUs using Arm CMSIS-NN acceleration, eliminating cross-framework conversions for microcontroller targets.
key_points: Uses ahead-of-time compiler passes to lower PyTorch operators into CMSIS-NN optimized kernels, targeting Scalar, DSP, and Helium/MVE capability tiers.
Employs PyTorch's PT2E quantization framework with a purpose-built quantizer to generate INT8 graphs matched to CMSIS-NN data layouts.
Achieves a minimal core runtime footprint under 20 KiB of flash using operator selective builds to link only required model operators.
Benchmarked four MLPerf Tiny models on an Alif Ensemble E8 single Cortex-M55 core, executing each model in 21.5 ms or less using under 90 KiB of RAM.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can now train, quantize, and deploy machine learning models to resource-constrained microcontrollers entirely within the native PyTorch ecosystem without model conversion tools.

infra.title: Day 0 support for Muse Spark Open on vLLM

summary.tldr: vLLM announced Day-0 serving support for Meta's Muse Spark Open, an 816B total/42B active parameter sparse MoE model featuring a 1M context window and multimodal perception.
key_points: Model architecture comprises an 816B parameter text decoder across 62 MoE layers, a 2B vision encoder, an audio encoder, and sandwich normalization.
Offered in BF16, NVFP4, and AMD MXFP4 quantizations, supported across NVIDIA, AMD, and initial TPU backends.
Supports advanced parallelism strategies including Tensor, Pipeline, Expert (EP), Tensor Expert (TEP), Dual Expert (DEP), and Prefill/Decode (PD) disaggregation.
Includes speculative decoding accelerated by a custom DSpark draft model using adaptive verification block rejection sampling.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, enterprise-scale inference and speculative acceleration of Meta's largest open-weights MoE model for long-horizon agentic coding across diverse hardware ecosystems.

infra.title: Announcing Day 0 Support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on vLLM

summary.tldr: vLLM announced day-zero serving support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B mixture-of-experts multimodal model designed for always-on agent workflows.
key_points: Model architecture uses a 120-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design with 12 billion active parameters (120B-A12B).
Supports multimodal inputs (text, images, documents, and video) alongside tool use and reasoning traces parsed via nemotron_v3.
vLLM features day-zero optimizations including continuous batching, prefix caching, OpenAI-compatible APIs, and NVFP4 target quantization for hardware like 1x GB200 setups.
Accelerates token generation in long-running workflows using Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding configured via --speculative-config.method mtp.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can deploy a single, low-precision multimodal agent model on vLLM with high generation speed and native video/document understanding without running separate vision and text pipelines.
